cards.text: Friend, grab your apron, because today we're baking with a SONG. David, Israel's king, sang it to the LORD on the day the LORD delivered him from the hand of all his enemies. And one more name gets its own spot at the end of that line.

cards.question: The LORD delivered David from all his enemies and from the hand of ___.

cards.text: Saul was Israel's king before David (1 Samuel 11:15). Then David opens with a pile of names for God: rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, stronghold, refuge, Savior, and friend, he is NOT stopping.

cards.question: Rock, fortress, stronghold, refuge. What do all of David's pictures for God have in common?
When David calls on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised, he says he'll be ___ from his enemies.

cards.text: Then David remembers how bad it got: the waves of death engulfed him, and the cords of Sheol tangled him up. Friend, I got tangled in rubber bands for YEARS in a junk drawer, and that was nothing like this.

cards.question: Death has David tangled up like cords. What does David do?

answers.text: He cries out to the LORD

cards.question: David's cry for help never makes it all the way to God.

cards.text: And THEN. The earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the heavens trembled.

cards.question: The earth and the heavens are shaking. What does David say is the reason?

cards.text: Smoke rises from His nostrils and consuming fire from His mouth. Then He parts the heavens and comes down with dark clouds beneath His feet, so hold on to your chef's hat, friend.

cards.question: In David's song, the LORD comes down riding a cherub and soaring on the wings of the wind.

cards.text: He makes darkness a canopy around Him, with thick clouds all around. Then the LORD thundered from heaven, and the voice of the Most High resounded.

cards.question: The LORD thunders from heaven, but David's foes hold their ground.

cards.text: He shot His arrows and hurled lightning, and the foes scattered. Then at the blast of the breath of His nostrils, the channels of the sea appeared and the foundations of the world were exposed.

cards.question: The sea is pulled back, and David is the one who was drowning in the waves of death. What does the LORD do?

answers.text: He reaches down and draws him out
He sends a ship to carry him off
He tells him to swim for the shore

cards.text: He rescued David from foes too mighty for him, and when they confronted him on his day of calamity, the LORD was his support. Friend, I lose fights to a jar lid, but DAVID admitting somebody was too strong for him? That's honest.

cards.question: The LORD brought David out into the open. Why does David say the LORD rescued him?

cards.text: Next David says the LORD has rewarded him according to his righteousness, according to the cleanness of his hands.

cards.question: David says the LORD rewarded him for his righteousness. What does David point to?

answers.text: He kept the ways of the LORD
He won every battle he fought
He built the LORD a temple

cards.question: David says he has set the LORD's statutes aside.

cards.text: He says he's been blameless before Him and kept himself from iniquity, so the LORD repaid him. Then David turns and speaks right to God about how He meets people.

cards.question: David says that to the faithful, God shows Himself faithful. So to the blameless, how does God show Himself?
David says that to the crooked, God shows Himself crooked too.

cards.text: Not crooked, friend. SHREWD. And David says You save an afflicted people, but Your eyes are on the haughty.

cards.question: God's eyes are on the haughty. What for?

cards.text: Then David says, "For You, O LORD, are my lamp; the LORD lights up my darkness." Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer begging for a crack of kitchen light, and David's got a light nobody can shut a drawer on.

cards.question: With the LORD lighting up his darkness, what does David say he can do?

answers.text: Charge an army and scale a wall
Rule the land without any help

cards.text: Then he sings, "As for God, His way is perfect; the word of the LORD is flawless." He is a shield to all who take refuge in Him.

cards.question: Next David asks two questions: Who is God besides the LORD? Who is the Rock except our God? What answer is he expecting?

cards.text: God is his strong fortress, and He makes David's feet like those of a deer and stations him upon the heights. Feet like a deer, friend? I stand on a gold base, I don't even HAVE feet, I just hop.

cards.question: God trains David's hands for ___.
With God's training, David says his arms can bend a bow of bronze.

cards.text: Then David says God has given him His shield of salvation. And right in the middle of all this battle talk comes a soft line.

cards.question: In the middle of all his battle talk, what does David say exalts him?
God broadens the path beneath David so that his ___ do not give way.

cards.text: Now David's on the move: he pursued his enemies and did not turn back until they were consumed, and they fell under his feet. No snooze button, friend. No five more minutes. He does NOT turn back.

cards.question: David chased his enemies down. Where does he say his strength for battle came from?

answers.text: The weapons he took from Saul

cards.text: God made David's enemies retreat before him. They looked around, but there was no one to save them.

cards.question: When David's enemies look to the LORD, He answers them.

cards.text: David says he crushed and trampled them like mud in the streets. Then he turns from the battlefield to his own people.

cards.question: David tells the LORD, You have delivered me from the ___ of my people.
God has kept David as the head of nations. How do foreigners act toward David?

answers.text: They march out to fight him

cards.text: Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds. Friend, that was ME every time the junk drawer opened: is this a rescue, or is this cleanup day?
And then David bursts into praise: "The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock!"

cards.question: Near the end of his song, David calls God by the same picture he started with: a rock.

cards.text: He's the God who avenges David and brings down nations beneath him. He frees David from his enemies and rescues him from violent men.

cards.question: Because of all this, David says he will ___ the LORD among the ___.

cards.text: Then the last line looks past David himself: "Great salvation He brings to His king."

cards.question: In the last line of David's song, who does God show loving devotion to?

answers.text: The soldiers who fought beside him

cards.question: In that last line, David is named as the LORD's anointed.

findings.problem: The question asks what 'all of David's pictures for God' have in common, and the right answer is 'Places to stay safe.' But card 3 also lists deliverer, shield and Savior, which aren't places, so the right answer isn't true for every picture the question covers.

rule.text: When a question covers more than one group, like the sea creatures and the birds, the right answer must be true for every group in it.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'pardoned' and 'banished' don't work in the sentence ('pardoned from his enemies,' 'banished from his enemies'), so 'saved' is the only answer that reads naturally and it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Card 5's question already says 'When David calls on the LORD,' which gives away the answer to card 7 ('He cries out to the LORD').

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'He sends a ship to carry him off' and 'He tells him to swim for the shore' read as silly next to the right answer, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the rescue line, the jar lid line, and 'That's honest.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card cites 2 Samuel 22:24-25, but its last sentence ('Then David turns and speaks right to God about how He meets people') tells the content of verse 26, which falls outside the cited range.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the fortress and deer line, 'Feet like a deer, friend?', and the gold base line.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'I don't even HAVE feet' adds a new physical fact about Papa Dorin that his character description never states.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: Story card 16 sets up the question with 'right in the middle of all this battle talk comes a soft line.' The word 'soft' points straight to 'God's gentleness' and rules out 'His own strength' and 'His army's courage.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: the pursuit line, 'No snooze button, friend.', 'No five more minutes.', and 'He does NOT turn back.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Story card 3 says 'there was no one to save them,' which gives away that the LORD does not answer the enemies.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Story card 9, right before this card, quotes 'blessed be my Rock!', which gives away that David calls God a rock near the end of the song.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Story card 13 says 'the last line looks past David himself,' which rules out 'David alone for his lifetime' and points to 'David and his descendants forever.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
